title: On the Expressive Power and Capacity of Quantum Data Reuploaders
abstract: Data reuploading---repeatedly encoding classical inputs at multiple layers of a parameterized quantum circuit---is a central mechanism for enhancing the expressivity of quantum neural networks (QNNs). Building on the Fourier-theoretic framework of Schuld et al.~\cite{schuld2021fourier}, we study the frequency spectrum of the general multivariate, $R$-reupload architecture (QDR). (i) We make explicit that the accessible frequencies form the set $K_R=S^{(R)}-S^{(R)}$, which equals the $R$-fold sumset $T^{(R)}$ of the difference set $T=S-S$ of the encoding spectrum, and we characterise it exactly: $K_R=\{k\in\mathcal L:\ \ell_T(k)\le R\}$, where $\mathcal L=\mathrm{span}_{\mathbb Z}(T)$ is an integer lattice and $\ell_T$ is word length in $T$. (ii) We show that the \emph{directions} of the spectrum stabilise already at $R=1$ (the real span of $K_R$ equals that of $\mathcal L$), whereas the spectrum itself never saturates: the maximal frequency grows linearly in $R$ and the number of frequencies grows polynomially, as $Θ(R^{m})$ with $m=\mathrm{rank}\,\mathcal L$. (iii) Using the spectrum size, we give a Rademacher-complexity bound on the capacity of QDRs of order $\sqrt{|K_R|/n}$. (iv) We report experiments on function approximation and classification with train/test splits, several seeds and parameter-matched classical baselines. The simulated spectra match the theory exactly. A single-qubit QDR beats a matched MLP on several smooth or periodic univariate targets and on the spiral task, but it is clearly worse on multivariate regression ($d\ge4$), where it is highly sensitive to the input-encoding scale; it beats the MLP only on equations with $d\le3$ inputs.

title: Sufficient quantum provenance: retained fields and certified recording precision
abstract: Which execution details must a quantum computation retain, and to what precision, to support a declared comparison? We define a sufficient record by the largest Hellinger distance between outcome laws that share it. Our main result is a circuit-derived certificate for continuous recording precision: independent channel-mixture probabilities enter through the affinity of latent noise flags, while coherent rotation differences enter through conditional quantum fidelity. Their joint composition bounds whole record cells without simulating their outcome distributions. For four-qubit QAOA at depth one, a 13-bit comparison record guarantees distance below 0.05 throughout a declared continuous noise box, uniformly over programmed angles when comparisons hold the logical task fixed. A construction with observable noise flags attains the general bound. Exact tensorization of Hellinger affinity connects recording precision to the length of a future measurement transcript. On finite context classes, separation witnesses certify minimum-cost field retention; a four-field record is the unique minimum for 28 archived QAOA instances. Fresh six-qubit processor measurements establish different minimum label counts at one common tolerance: two labels are necessary and sufficient for raw laws, while one suffices after a fixed decoder for a synthetic image-segmentation task. These hardware conclusions are conditional on stationary independent shots and remain distinct from the analytic channel certificate. Shared task definitions and evidential archives are retained separately. The framework specifies which execution distinctions matter, how precisely to record them, and what evidence supports the resulting agreement guarantee.

title: EC-EarthFlow: Probabilistic emulation of daily transient global climate model simulations with flow matching
abstract: We introduce EC-EarthFlow, a generative flow matching model that emulates simulations from the physical climate model EC-Earth3. The model is trained on transient simulations from EC-Earth3 (1950-2166, SSP2-4.5) to predict the day ahead temperature field from the previous days temperature as well as annual mean temperature. Predictions are made auto-regressively with rollout periods of between a month and an extended season. Using only this variable of interest, we are able to reproduce the daily variability, spatial patterns, annual cycle and long-term trend from EC-Earth3 at a substantially lower computational cost than the physical model. We demonstrate that EC-EarthFlow is stable for long inference periods, and that it can learn the physical relationships as simulated in EC-Earth3.

title: emg2face: Expressive Facial Animation with High-Density Surface EMG
abstract: Facial movements convey subtle and important information that is critical for human social communication. Optical methods for face capture are difficult or impossible to use when the face is occluded by head-mounted devices (HMDs), such as VR headsets. Even with a clear line of sight, such methods raise privacy concerns and require head-mounted capture rigs that offset cameras and lighting from the face. We show that high-density surface electromyography (HD-sEMG) provides a viable non-optical alternative that addresses these challenges. We measured 64 EMG channels, using two textile EMG grids, with 32 from the forehead (typically occluded by an HMD) and 32 from the side of the face. EMG data were digitized at 2048 Hz and filtered. Facial movements were simultaneously recorded and used to estimate 478 3D facial landmarks using MediaPipe's Face Landmarker. A major challenge in such multimodal recordings is synchronizing EMG and video data, which have different sampling frequencies and independent clocks. We developed a novel synchronization method using analog audio bursts that is capable of sub-millisecond synchronization. We also developed a staged fitting method that fits a recent high-resolution parametric head model (GNM), with 253 identity blendshapes and 383 expression blendshapes, to the MediaPipe landmarks as participants performed different facial expressions. We trained a deep neural network comprising per-grid spatial encoders followed by a dilated temporal convolutional network (TCN) to predict blendshape parameters from HD-sEMG signals at 100 Hz. Once trained, the network can predict expression blendshapes solely from HD-sEMG recordings. The output can be rendered using standard real-time blendshape animation methods. We demonstrate the methods using recordings from 25 participants, and direct expression transfer to a variety of human faces and non-human characters.

title: Hate speech recognition in social media through speech transcription using deep neural networks
abstract: Η συνεχής αύξηση του περιεχομένου που δημοσιεύεται καθημερινά στα μέσα κοινωνικής δικτύωσης έχει οδηγήσει στην εξάπλωση φαινομένων όπως η ρητορική μίσους, καθιστώντας αναγκαία την ανάπτυξη αυτοματοποιημένων συστημάτων ανίχνευσης επιβλαβούς περιεχομένου. Σκοπός της παρούσας διπλωματικής εργασίας είναι η ανάπτυξη ενός συστήματος αναγνώρισης σχολίων ρητορικής μίσους με χρήση της τεχνολογίας Speech-to-Text, αξιοποιώντας τεχνικές Βαθιάς Μάθησης (Deep Learning) και Επεξεργασίας Φυσικής Γλώσσας (Natural Language Processing). Αρχικά, για την μετατροπή των λέξεων σε αριθμητικές αναπαραστάσεις χρησιμοποιήθηκε το GloVe word embedding. Στη συνέχεια, σχεδιάστηκε και εκπαιδεύτηκε ένα νευρωνικό δίκτυο Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), το οποίο επιλέχθηκε λόγω της ικανότητάς του να μοντελοποιεί ακολουθίες κειμένου και να διατηρεί πληροφορία μακροπρόθεσμων εξαρτήσεων. Για τη βελτιστοποίηση της αρχιτεκτονικής του μοντέλου εφαρμόζεται η μέθοδος Bayesian Optimization, η οποία χρησιμοποιείται για την αυτόματη επιλογή των κατάλληλων υπερπαραμέτρων. Επιπλέον, για τη μετατροπή του προφορικού λόγου σε κείμενο επιλέχθηκε το μοντέλο Faster-Whisper, λόγω της υψηλής ταχύτητας και της αποτελεσματικότητάς του στη φωνητική μεταγραφή. Η αξιολόγηση πραγματοποιείται με χρήση των μετρικών Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, καθώς και μέσω του πίνακα σύγχυσης (Confusion Matrix) και των καμπυλών ROC-AUC. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι το μοντέλο παρουσιάζει ικανοποιητική ικανότητα γενίκευσης, επιτυγχάνοντας ακρίβεια εκπαίδευσης (Train Accuracy) 78%, ακρίβεια επικύρωσης (Validation Accuracy) 74% και ακρίβεια δοκιμής (Test Accuracy) 70%. Επιπλέον, παρουσιάζει αποτελεσματική διάκριση μεταξύ σχολίων που περιέχουν ρητορική μίσους και σχολίων που δεν περιέχουν, επιτυγχάνοντας F1-Score περίπου 79% στο σύνολο εκπαίδευσης και 74% στο σύνολο δοκιμής, και AUC περίπου 0.75 στο σύνολο δοκιμής. Τέλος, η κύρια συνεισφορά της εργασίας βασίζεται στον συνδυασμό της αρχιτεκτονικής LSTM με τη βελτιστοποίηση υπερπαραμέτρων μέσω Bayesian Optimization, προσφέροντας μια αποδοτική προσέγγιση για την ανίχνευση ρητορικής μίσους σε δεδομένα κοινωνικών δικτύων.

Αρχικά, για την μετατροπή των λέξεων σε αριθμητικές αναπαραστάσεις χρησιμοποιήθηκε το GloVe word embedding. Στη συνέχεια, σχεδιάστηκε και εκπαιδεύτηκε ένα νευρωνικό δίκτυο Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), το οποίο επιλέχθηκε λόγω της ικανότητάς του να μοντελοποιεί ακολουθίες κειμένου και να διατηρεί πληροφορία μακροπρόθεσμων εξαρτήσεων. Για τη βελτιστοποίηση της αρχιτεκτονικής του μοντέλου εφαρμόζεται η μέθοδος Bayesian Optimization, η οποία χρησιμοποιείται για την αυτόματη επιλογή των κατάλληλων υπερπαραμέτρων. Επιπλέον, για τη μετατροπή του προφορικού λόγου σε κείμενο επιλέχθηκε το μοντέλο Faster-Whisper, λόγω της υψηλής ταχύτητας και της αποτελεσματικότητάς του στη φωνητική μεταγραφή. Η αξιολόγηση πραγματοποιείται με χρήση των μετρικών Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, καθώς και μέσω του πίνακα σύγχυσης (Confusion Matrix) και των καμπυλών ROC-AUC. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι το μοντέλο παρουσιάζει ικανοποιητική ικανότητα γενίκευσης, επιτυγχάνοντας ακρίβεια εκπαίδευσης (Train Accuracy) 78%, ακρίβεια επικύρωσης (Validation Accuracy) 74% και ακρίβεια δοκιμής (Test Accuracy) 70%. Επιπλέον, παρουσιάζει αποτελεσματική διάκριση μεταξύ σχολίων που περιέχουν ρητορική μίσους και σχολίων που δεν περιέχουν, επιτυγχάνοντας F1-Score περίπου 79% στο σύνολο εκπαίδευσης και 74% στο σύνολο δοκιμής, και AUC περίπου 0.75 στο σύνολο δοκιμής. Τέλος, η κύρια συνεισφορά της εργασίας βασίζεται στον συνδυασμό της αρχιτεκτονικής LSTM με τη βελτιστοποίηση υπερπαραμέτρων μέσω Bayesian Optimization, προσφέροντας μια αποδοτική προσέγγιση για την ανίχνευση ρητορικής μίσους σε δεδομένα κοινωνικών δικτύων.

title: IA na manutenção e instalação
abstract: IA na manutenção e instalação apresenta um percurso de aplicação de inteligência artificial para eletricistas, encanadores, instaladores e assistência técnica.O objetivo do livro é ajudar o leitor a qualificar solicitações, reduzir retrabalho e entregar serviços com escopo e comunicação claros. O conteúdo usa casos didáticos fictícios, exemplos e propostas de trabalho para discutir decisões, organização de informações e revisão humana.Ao longo dos 10 capítulos, você encontrará:O custo do orçamento incompletoRecepção de solicitaçõesPerguntas úteis antes da visitaEscopo e proposta com IAAgenda e preparação de materiaisO percurso avança até Projeto: do primeiro contato ao serviço concluído. As atividades devem ser adaptadas ao contexto e conferidas pelo leitor; os casos fictícios não representam resultados comprovados. Edição digital em EPUB. Página do livro: https://edu.cog.ia.br/livros/manutencao-instalacao/ . O arquivo integral tem acesso restrito; os metadados e o DOI são públicos.

title: Independent external validation of virtual multiplex immunofluorescence from H&E reveals that predicted channels encode tissue composition rather than cell identity
abstract: This record contains the analysis code and derived results for an independent external validation of GigaTIME, a deep-learning model that predicts 23-channel virtual multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) from a single haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) whole-slide image. What is included - analysis/ - Python pipeline for tile extraction, reproduction of the official colour-normalisation and channel-decoding protocol, model inference, and metric computation. - analysis/results/ - the derived result files (JSON) that underlie every figure, table and reported statistic in the manuscript. - figures/ - publication-quality figure files (PDF and PNG). - docs/ - dataset accession list, reproduction instructions and environment specification. Validation layers 1. Pixel level: 945 HEMIT patches. 2. Spot level: 15,489 spots from GSE230424. 3. Patient level: 222 TCGA-THCA samples with matched RPPA protein measurements. 4. Single-cell level: 994,729 cells from 41 ORION-CRC patients. Companion manuscript: "Independent external validation of virtual multiplex immunofluorescence from H&E reveals that predicted channels encode tissue composition rather than cell identity" (under review). Licence: MIT. No primary data are redistributed here; all third-party datasets are identified by accession and must be obtained from their original sources.

title: Quantum Computing in Manufacturing: From Today's Capabilities to Tomorrow's Impact
abstract: The threshold of the second quantum revolution has been reached; wherein isolated quantum systems are being utilized for macroscopic applications. With the exponential scaling of quantum computers and cross-industry milestones such as the goal of delivering fault-tolerant systems with 200 logical qubits and 100 million gates by 2029 entirely new possibilities in computing are emerging. In production engineering, the growing complexity and interconnectivity of dynamic manufacturing processes, combined with the vast data volumes generated by digital twins, will soon demand computing capabilities beyond what classical architectures can efficiently provide. At present, quantum hardware does not yet have computing power or error-free operation required for complex industrial applications. However, the immense scaling potential offered by quantum effects makes it indispensable for manufacturing technology. The presentation introduces fundamentals of quantum hardware, compares physical qubit realizations, and explains the core quantum principles. The manipulation of quantum states is achieved via unary and binary gates. Complex industrial applications, such as the optimization of logistics and process chains, are expected to require more than 1,000 error-corrected qubits. Hardware-software co-design is thus essential. In the field of production engineering, the development and validation of application-specific algorithms for these future quantum systems must therefore begin now. As an exemplary case study for these future areas of research, this presentation will show the evaluation of quantum computing in digital twins using the example of a drilling process analysis based on Bayesian inference. For root-cause analysis, high-frequency NC signal data (currents, jerk, contour deviations) from 264 boreholes were processed. This probabilistic model for identifying causes is mapped as a Quantum Bayesian Network (12 qubits) on a quantum circuit. Because exact Bayesian inference is known to be #P-complete, it is considered a highly promising candidate for future quantum advantages in manufacturing research. Comparing classical hardware, quantum simulators (Qiskit), and real quantum hardware (IBM Hanoi) reveal current limitations but also significant future potential. Current NISQ systems still exhibit substantial deviations (maximum absolute error sometimes over 60%) when processing such networks, primarily due to limited qubit connectivity, the lack of native multi-controlled rotation gates, and the challenges of non-binary discretization. Nevertheless, the successful use of quantum simulators with errors below 3% proves that the development and validation of practical quantum algorithms are already possible and highly beneficial today. © 2026 The Authors. title: An Improved Online Latent Dirichlet Allocation Model with Adaptive Topic Inheritance for Hot Event Mining and Evolution Tracking
abstract: Aiming at hot event mining and evolutionary tracking over temporal text streams, this paper proposes an Improved Online Latent Dirichlet Allocation (IOLDA) model integrated with the topic inheritance mechanism to address the drawbacks of the original Online Latent Dirichlet Allocation (OLDA), including fixed historical weights, semantic confusion between emerging and legacy topics, and global vocabulary expansion. Based on the first-order Markov assumption, the IOLDA model takes the topic-word distribution of the previous time slice as the modeling prior and dynamically adjusts inheritance factors according to topic popularity to assign different inheritance strengths to historical semantics. Parameters are only transmitted over the intersection vocabulary of adjacent slices to reduce computational overhead induced by vocabulary expansion. This paper adopts symmetric Jensen–Shannon (JS) divergence to quantify semantic discrepancies between topics across adjacent slices and distinguishes three evolutionary states: topic persistence, extinction, and mutation. Subsequently, homologous topics are linked across time slices to construct event evolution chains. Same-index topic pairs are treated as candidate temporal links and retained only after JS-based semantic validation. On Reuters-21578, IOLDA reduces perplexity from 1039.6 to 1011.7 and increases coherence score from 0.454 to 0.476 relative to OLDA. Average alignment accuracy rises from 0.817 to 0.859, while controlled emerging topic F1 rises from 0.818 to 0.854 and delay falls from 0.88 to 0.56 slices. Efficiency results show lower overall time and memory use and higher throughput. Findings are limited to the datasets and setting and do not establish universal superiority over multi-window OLDA, explicit matching methods, or alternative new-word priors.

title: Fortifying Foundation Models: Fine-Tuning for Robustness, Compositionality and Safety
abstract: This thesis addresses the critical challenges hindering the safe and reliable de- ployment of modern vision models and foundation models, specifically image classifiers, Vision-Language Models (VLMs), Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), and Large Lan- guage Models (LLMs). We investigate four interconnected domains essential for trustworthy AI: establishing strong adversarial robustness in both discriminative image classifiers and multi-modal systems, improving compositional reasoning, and establishing mechanisms for unlearning to mitigate harmful, outdated, or unintended behaviors, thereby strengthening model reliability and accountability. While training massive models from scratch is often computationally prohibitive, we demonstrate that targeted adaptations of pre-trained models can eﬀectively resolve these challenges without compromising their general capabilities. Our first contribution revisits adversarial training for modern ImageNet architectures. Prior work on adversarially robust image classifiers focused almost exclusively on ResNets and small datasets like CIFAR-10, leaving open how modern architectures such as Vision Transformers (ViTs) and ConvNeXts behave under adversarial training on ImageNet. We show that seemingly minor architectural choices, most notably replacing the standard patch-based input stem with a convolutional stem, combined with strong clean pre-training and heavy data augmentation, have a large and consistent impact on the achieved robustness. Crucially, these changes not only improve robustness in the threat model seen at training time, but substantially improve generalization to unseen ℓ1 and ℓ2 threat models, a problem that had received little attention before. Our second contribution centers on adversarial robustness in multi-modal systems. We robustify the vision encoder of CLIP models, making them capable of defending against visual adversaries using an unsupervised fine-tuning technique. Crucially, we demonstrate that this robustness transfers to downstream LVLMs, securing them against stealth attacks where malicious image manipulations aim to deceive users. Beyond model robustness, we establish that these adversarially robust encoders serve as superior perceptual metrics that are better aligned with humans, resilient to manipulation, and essential for reliable content filtering and dataset curation in real-world applications. In the third contribution, we tackle the limitations of compositional reasoning in vision- language models. While current models excel at recognizing individual objects, they often fail to grasp the nuanced relationships between the objects in the image. This deficiency can lead to failure modes which propagate to downstream LVLMs that inherit these problems through frozen encoders. We introduce CLIC (Compositionally-aware Learning in CLIP), 1 a method that enhances both lexical sensitivity and semantic understanding. By refining how the model processes complex relationships, CLIC improves the compositional reasoning abilities of the encoder, which is vital for the performance of downstream LVLMs that rely on CLIP for visual understanding. Finally, we address reliability, privacy and compliance in Large Language Models through unlearning, the selective removal of specific knowledge. We introduce JensUn, a novel framework leveraging Jensen-Shannon Divergence to achieve stable knowledge removal while preserving the model’s general ability. To rigorously benchmark progress in this nascent field, we introduce LPF (Less Prominent Facts), a curated dataset of niche topics, and an evaluation protocol that takes the worst case over diﬀerent query formats using an LLM as a semantic judge. These evaluations reveal significant flaws in existing unlearning methods, highlighting the need for the more robust approach oﬀered by JensUn. Collectively, these works reveal fundamental connections between seemingly disparate chal- lenges. The robustness techniques used for adversarial defense in both classifiers and multi- modal models share conceptual roots, as both require the model to distinguish between valid and malicious patterns. Similarly, the knowledge manipulation required for unlearning in LLMs parallels the targeted parameter adjustments studied across all our robustness work. This thesis suggests that the principles of safety and reliability, whether in robustness, reasoning, or privacy, span across modalities and architectures.

title: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
abstract: Abstract Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have largely been driven by large language models, deep neural networks that operate over discrete units called tokens. To represent text, most large language models use words or word fragments as the tokens, known as subword tokenization 1 . Subword tokenization obscures fine-grained information, which is problematic, especially for scientific data—such as computer code or biological sequences—where meaning depends on the individual characters or bytes 2 . Models that instead operate directly on the byte encoding of text avoid these limitations, but until now they have lagged behind subword-based models in performance. Here we introduce a general method for creating byte-level large language models through byteification that approach the capabilities of subword-based systems. We use a two-stage conversion procedure to retrofit existing subword-based models into byte-level models with minimal extra training. The resulting models outperform earlier byte-level approaches and excel on character-level reasoning tasks, achieving practical inference speeds by efficiently processing byte-level information and adaptability by reusing the existing ecosystem around the source large language model. Our results remove a long-standing performance barrier to end-to-end byte-level language modelling, demonstrating that models operating on raw text encodings can scale competitively while offering advantages in domains requiring fine-grained textual understanding.

title: ECHO: Embodied Camera Observations of Human Object Carrying
abstract: Embodied and assistive agents must do more than recognize objects: they must reason about where an object belongs given the layout of an environment and the habits of the people who live in it. Progress on this problem has been limited, in part because no dedicated benchmark or dataset exists to define and evaluate it. Existing RGB-D scan datasets reconstruct static rooms without human activity, while human-object-interaction datasets capture motion without a navigable, fully reconstructed scene or a ground-truth notion of an object's natural destination. We introduce contextual object placement as a benchmark task: predicting an object's destination during an observed object-carrying episode. To support this task, we present Embodied Camera observations of Human Object carrying (ECHO), a large-scale synthetic dataset that pairs dense RGB-D scans of indoor scenes with recordings of an embodied human carrying everyday objects to context-appropriate destinations. ECHO is the first publicly available dataset to combine reconstructed scenes, human activity, natural language, and contextual-placement annotations. It comprises 3,805 human-annotated episodes across 159 floors of 115 HM3D scenes, involving 198 distinct objects. Each floor includes a complete RGB-D scan with human-annotated room labels and a surface list. Each episode provides synchronized RGB-D encounter clips; 6-DoF camera, human, and object trajectories; start and destination surfaces; an action caption; and a human-written context: a single sentence describing the inhabitant's routine that implies the destination without naming it. We evaluate contextual object placement using input-masked probes and an end-to-end baseline. Results show that no single input modality is sufficient, highlighting the need to jointly reason over scene structure, human activity, and contextual knowledge.

Existing RGB-D scan datasets reconstruct static rooms without human activity, while human-object-interaction datasets capture motion without a navigable, fully reconstructed scene or a ground-truth notion of an object's natural destination. We introduce contextual object placement as a benchmark task: predicting an object's destination during an observed object-carrying episode. To support this task, we present Embodied Camera observations of Human Object carrying (ECHO), a large-scale synthetic dataset that pairs dense RGB-D scans of indoor scenes with recordings of an embodied human carrying everyday objects to context-appropriate destinations. ECHO is the first publicly available dataset to combine reconstructed scenes, human activity, natural language, and contextual-placement annotations. It comprises 3,805 human-annotated episodes across 159 floors of 115 HM3D scenes, involving 198 distinct objects. Each floor includes a complete RGB-D scan with human-annotated room labels and a surface list. Each episode provides synchronized RGB-D encounter clips; 6-DoF camera, human, and object trajectories; start and destination surfaces; an action caption; and a human-written context: a single sentence describing the inhabitant's routine that implies the destination without naming it. We evaluate contextual object placement using input-masked probes and an end-to-end baseline. Results show that no single input modality is sufficient, highlighting the need to jointly reason over scene structure, human activity, and contextual knowledge.

title: LLM Persuasion Is in the Eye of the Evaluation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have already been shown to match or exceed human experts in persuasion. While their persuasive capabilities hold promise for beneficial uses such as education and health communication, they can also be used to manipulate and misinform, making their evaluation a growing priority for developers and regulators. That evaluation, however, remains fragmented: studies differ in what they treat as persuasion, and broad claims often rest on narrow, situation-specific assessments. Automated methods, often modelled on human studies, offer a way to compare such assessments directly, as they can be run on the same models at scale and can include high-risk forms of persuasion that would be difficult or unethical to test on people. In this study, we adapt nine published automated methods to a shared setup, run them on the same fifteen LLMs, and ask whether their rankings agree and why. We find that the methods agree only weakly (mean Spearman $ρ= 0.25$). Our analyses point to two contributing factors. Models that refuse some tasks but not others, directly or indirectly, lower agreement by about a quarter, and these refusals fall mostly on manipulation tasks. General capability also plays a part: most rational persuasion (non-manipulative) methods track it, whereas most manipulation methods do not. Together, these findings suggest that agreement depends more on the task a method sets than on how it scores persuasion, although this pattern is only indicative given the eight methods available for analysis. More broadly, our results suggest that persuasion scores combine a model's ability to persuade with its willingness to do so. A single score is therefore informative about its own setting, but says little about a model's persuasiveness across tasks.

title: LiG-DETR: Local-in-Global Reassembly in Latent Space for Aerial Object Detection
abstract: Aerial object detection faces substantial scale and density variations. Small objects are easily degraded by downsampling and feature compression, while medium and large objects require sufficient global context. Existing methods mainly follow two paradigms: image slicing provides clearer local evidence but relies on independent crop-level prediction and post-processing, whereas feature- and query-level optimization preserves unified inference but operates on already compressed full-image representations, limiting recovery of fine-grained information. This raises a key question: can aerial detection directly acquire high-fidelity local evidence before feature degradation and integrate it into a unified end-to-end framework? To this end, we propose LiG-DETR, an Efficient Global-Local Reassembly framework that reformulates image slicing as high-fidelity local feature acquisition. A shared encoder extracts global and locally magnified features, which are projected into the detector feature space. The projected local features are reassembled according to their original spatial locations to form a globally aligned local feature level, and a single DETR decoder jointly decodes global and local features. To reduce redundant computation, Context-Preserved Selective Reassembly focuses high-resolution encoding on informative regions while preserving a dense feature layout, and Density-Aware Adaptive Query Allocation adapts the decoder query budget using encoder proposal scores. Experiments show substantial gains on small and medium objects while retaining strong large-object performance, with favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs and improved cross-domain generalization. The code will be released.

title: AFP-Enterprise: Evaluating Host-Level Runtime Containment for Planner–Tool Execution
abstract: AFP-Enterprise is a host runtime kernel beside a local planner, reached by a synchronous pre-flight probe. Before irreversible tool I/O, the planner reports recursion depth and con text, then blocks on allow, delay, or isolate. The kernel does not parse prompts or tool schemas. It checks, in order, an emergency stop, a depth cap, a four-axis pressure maxi mum, and a specified isolate–recover state machine. On a personal computer, a LangGraph planner issued real lookup and loopback HTTP GET calls. Five bounded jobs completed under no gate, a per-step wipe, and the current sidecar (false isolate = 0). A scripted loop and a 48-task burst ran to completion without a gate and were contained by both gated variants. Those traces fire the depth cap and the hard pressure isolate; they do not reach the delay band or the recover machine. The gated variants differ only when a later probe reuses leftover host telemetry: AFP-Enterprise refuses; the wipe allows. A new job that reports depth 0 is admitted under both. Two planners on one sidecar can overwrite each other, so the kernel keeps last-reported host telemetry, not a lock on who the planner is. The measured increment is retained execution telemetry, not identity-locked persistence, production safety, or LLM-agent validation. A 500-node Monte Carlo in the appendix is a breaker invariant, not a field result.

title: Funktionale Workspace-Strukturen in Sprachmodellen: Offene Forschungsanfrage mit Forschungsübersicht
abstract: In der laufenden Forschung zu leistungsfähigen KI-Modellen wurde eine emergente, nicht eigens programmierte Struktur beschrieben, die den funktionalen Anforderungen eines Global Workspace entspricht. Die Global Workspace Theory ist eine einflussreiche neurowissenschaftliche Theorie darüber, wie Informationen für verschiedene kognitive Prozesse verfügbar werden. Anthropic nennt die in seinen Modellen gefundene Struktur J-Space. Die Studie zeigt, dass sie am internen Reasoning beteiligt ist. Zur Einordnung des Befunds und der seitherigen Forschungslage bittet diese Anfrage Frontier-Entwickler und KI-Forschende um fachliche Rückmeldung.

title: Digital Guest Experience (CX) – Navigating the Shift from SEO to GEO
abstract: Chapter 14 is the first of two chapters in Part Six that concentrates on the digital and extended frontier of new technology in hospitality. In Chapter 14 , we look at the guest experience (UX or CX) and how things are shifting from SEO (search engine optimisation) to GEO (generative engine optimisation) or, in other words, how people search and research behaviours are shifting from a simple online search with Google to the use of AI to do everything from placing orders for deliveries to making hotel reservations. This chapter looks specifically at how to conduct a Digital CX Audit and goes on to offer a 90-day roadmap to improvement in this area, illustrated with real-world examples and finally an action sheet.

title: When Virtual Worlds Become Intelligent: Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality, and New Research Opportunities
abstract: The recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) have contributed to a significant visibility of generative AI. Despite the big spotlights being on AI nowadays, the ambition to develop computational systems capable of creating the illusion of intelligent behaviour is not new. One can date AI to the 1950s, when various researchers raised the topic and made remarkable contributions to the field’s establishment and evolution.

title: Masked Generative Motion Planning with Geometry-Guided Token Search
abstract: Generative motion planners typically use learned trajectory priors for initial generation, while leaving test-time repair to local continuous refinement. We introduce Masked Generative Motion Planning (MGMP), which extends the learned prior from efficient parallel generation to structural repair. A masked generative transformer generates discrete trajectory candidates in parallel, and Geometry-Guided Token Search (GGTS) uses scene geometry to target where to edit and which prior-supported alternatives to evaluate. This turns refinement into an efficient search over discrete motion alternatives, enabling route-level restructuring beyond local trajectory deformation. MGMP achieves 96% success on Ring Maze and 82% repair success on Controlled Route Invalidation on Kuka, exceeding the strongest external baselines by 23 and 25 percentage points, respectively. It further generalizes to unseen layouts, additional obstacles, unseen geometries, single- and dual-arm planning, and real-world Baxter tasks.

title: Benchmarking Adult Addressee Classification Across Child- and Adult-Directed Speech Datasets
abstract: In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of classification performance for distinguishing child-directed speech (CDS) from adult-directed speech (ADS) using speech data from corpora containing natural in-lab and in-the-wild CDS and ADS. We establish classification benchmarks for these datasets using self-supervised learning (SSL) representations, along with a range of time-pooled representations that go beyond first- and second-order statistics by incorporating cross-channel covariances in high-dimensional embeddings. In addition, we probe these representations to examine how different pooling methods capture prosodic information using linear probes. Overall, SSL-based representations prove particularly effective, achieving the best performance, while different pooling methods offer complementary advantages for the task.

title: SpikingVLA: Asynchronous Spiking Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: ANN-to-SNN conversion offers a practical route toward energy-efficient spiking Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models by bypassing the substantial cost of training large-scale SNNs from scratch. However, existing methods often require many timesteps to maintain competitive performance, resulting in substantial inference latency for real-time VLA deployment. To address this challenge, we introduce SpikingVLA, an ANN-to-SNN conversion framework that enables accurate and low-latency spiking VLA inference. Specifically, we propose a Dendritic Integrate-and-Fire (DIF) neuron that alleviates channel-wise activation outliers through dendritic mixing and adaptive somatic firing, enabling accurate ANN-to-SNN conversion with fewer timesteps. Building on DIF neurons, we further introduce an asynchronous execution mechanism that overlaps temporal computation across VLA components, reducing synchronization overhead and latency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SpikingVLA achieves competitive navigation performance with substantially improved inference efficiency. Compared with existing spiking VLA methods, SpikingVLA improves SR and SPL by 11.9\% and 12.6\%, respectively, while reducing first-action latency by 11.2$\times$. These results establish SpikingVLA as a practical framework for deploying pretrained VLA models with high-performance and low-latency spiking inference.

title: The AI Evaluation Ecosystem
abstract: AI evaluation shapes the decisions of model providers, users, funders, and regulators. We argue that designing valid benchmarks requires contextualizing design choices in the dynamics of this ecosystem of actors. We develop a simulation architecture that combines rule-based market dynamics with LLM-driven strategic actors, building on advances in Generative Agent-Based Modeling (GABM). We model benchmarks, consumer needs, and provider capabilities as vectors over a six-dimensional capability space (reasoning, coding, knowledge, safety, communication, agentic), with structural information partitions across actors. As a case study, we apply this stylized simulation to explore benchmark holdout design. We find that moving from public benchmarks to private holdout benchmarks shrinks the gap between benchmark scores and user satisfaction on most benchmarks but widens it on a few, depending on where holdout weights shift scoring credit. We stress-test our findings at both the instrument and case-study level, drawing on the V&V framework of Sargent (2013) and GABM-specific evidence criteria. Beyond holdout design, our simulation is a hypothesis-generating sandbox for studying how evaluator and policy choices, in turn, reshape the ecosystem.

title: Encrypted Traffic Classification with Deep Learning
abstract: Moderní bezpečnostní protokoly, jako jsou TLS 1.3, QUIC, Encrypted Client Hello a šifrované DNS, výrazně omezují množství informací dostupných při pasivním sledování síťového provozu. V důsledku toho se postupně snižuje účinnost tradičních přístupů k monitorování založených na inspekci obsahu komunikace, analýze nešifrovaných polí z průběhu navazování spojení a identifikaci podle doménových jmen. Přestože tyto technologie významně přispívají k ochraně soukromí uživatelů a důvěrnosti jejich komunikace, současně představují výzvu pro správce sítí odpovědné za jejich provoz a bezpečnost. Tato disertační práce se proto zaměřuje na návrh klasifikačních metod, které využívají výhradně informace z postranních kanálů síťové komunikace, konkrétně velikosti a směry paketů a časové intervaly mezi nimi. Výzkum vychází z dat získaných v páteřní síti ve spolupráci se sdružením CESNET, které provozuje národní výzkumnou a vzdělávací e-infrastrukturu. Práce tak propojuje reálná provozní data, systematické vyhodnocení navržených metod a moderní přístupy hlubokého učení pro řešení úlohy klasifikace šifrovaného síťového provozu.

title: From Observation to Action: Diagnosing Reference Gaps in Sequential Decision Problems
abstract: A controller may underperform a strong reference action for at least two fundamentally different reasons. The available observation may carry little detectable information about that action, or useful information may be present but not converted into a competent policy. We formulate this distinction as a diagnostic framework for sequential decision problems and apply it to two locked surrogate environments: a multistable continuous stirred-tank reactor (CSTR) and a jet-injection plant. The reference action is a grid-best safe action or a mass selected under a locked cost; it is not asserted to be a global oracle. The supplied analysis describes a one-dimensional additive Kraskov–Stögbauer–Grassberger (KSG) proxy with a permutation null and reports (\widehat I\approx0) for the CSTR and (\widehat I=0.621) nats for the jet. The CSTR result is consistent with an information-limited regime under the tested representation and power, not proof of independence. In the jet, positive association coexists with memory-enriched control that fails to improve on the factory baseline, locating the observed failure downstream of association without identifying its exact cause. Action-resolution checks preserve this contrast. The empirical contribution is therefore a layered diagnosis, not a universal information barrier: persistence does not entail extractability, and detectable information does not entail utility. We state the relevant assumptions, distinguish formal results from empirical observations, and provide a small synthetic, reproducible proof-of-concept that illustrates the logic without claiming to reproduce the plant experiments.Keywords: mutual information; sequential decision-making; KSG; permutation test; policy extraction; memory; safe control; oracle gap

title: Contextual Transduction Principle (CTP) : A Domain-Independent Systemic Architecture for Context-, State-, Projection-, Criterion-, and Medium-Conditioned Transformation
abstract: This paper proposes the Contextual Transduction Principle (CTP), a domain-independent systems framework for describing how an interaction or input is transformed by a system under a configuration consisting of internal state, relevant history, prior projection, external context, active criterion, and operative medium. The central claim is deliberately weaker than a universal empirical law: the same observable input need not have the same systemic effect when the processing configuration changes.The framework is designed to remain independent of any particular criterion, medium, discipline, or ontological class of system. Security, correctness, efficiency, morality, humour, classification, stability, utility, and other criteria therefore appear only as instantiations of a general criterion variable rather than as primitive commitments of the theory. Likewise, language, biological signalling, computation, social interaction, mechanical control, network communication, and symbolic processing can be represented as different media instantiating the same formal architecture.The paper develops four interconnected layers: phenomenological, epistemological, systemic-cybernetic, and mathematical-computational. A primary "haha" reaction case is used only as an illustrative phenomenon and is explicitly prevented from defining the theory's domain. Formal state-transition, discrepancy, projection, functional change, divergence, stochastic, continuous-time, and network formulations are derived. Falsifiability is addressed through controlled comparisons and null models. Forty compact cross-domain case instantiations are provided as model templates, not as empirical confirmations. Synthetic simulation methodology is specified to demonstrate logical behavior without confusing simulation with evidence about the real world.The principal contribution claimed here is not the general observation that context matters. That observation has substantial precedent. The proposed contribution is the explicit integration of input, prior projection, state, contextual configuration, criterion, and medium into a single operational transduction architecture with domain-independent variables, measurable discrepancy terms, boundary conditions, null cases, and cross-domain falsification requirements.

evidence.title: Contextual Transduction Principle (CTP) : A Domain-Independent Systemic Architecture for Context-, State-, Projection-, Criterion-, and Medium-Conditioned Transformation
evidence.abstract: This paper proposes the Contextual Transduction Principle (CTP), a domain-independent systems framework for describing how an interaction or input is transformed by a system under a configuration consisting of internal state, relevant history, prior projection, external context, active criterion, and operative medium. The central claim is deliberately weaker than a universal empirical law: the same observable input need not have the same systemic effect when the processing configuration changes.The framework is designed to remain independent of any particular criterion, medium, discipline, or ontological class of system. Security, correctness, efficiency, morality, humour, classification, stability, utility, and other criteria therefore appear only as instantiations of a general criterion variable rather than as primitive commitments of the theory. Likewise, language, biological signalling, computation, social interaction, mechanical control, network communication, and symbolic processing can be represented as different media instantiating the same formal architecture.The paper develops four interconnected layers: phenomenological, epistemological, systemic-cybernetic, and mathematical-computational. A primary "haha" reaction case is used only as an illustrative phenomenon and is explicitly prevented from defining the theory's domain. Formal state-transition, discrepancy, projection, functional change, divergence, stochastic, continuous-time, and network formulations are derived. Falsifiability is addressed through controlled comparisons and null models. Forty compact cross-domain case instantiations are provided as model templates, not as empirical confirmations. Synthetic simulation methodology is specified to demonstrate logical behavior without confusing simulation with evidence about the real world.The principal contribution claimed here is not the general observation that context matters. That observation has substantial precedent. The proposed contribution is the explicit integration of input, prior projection, state, contextual configuration, criterion, and medium into a single operational transduction architecture with domain-independent variables, measurable discrepancy terms, boundary conditions, null cases, and cross-domain falsification requirements.

title: "AI Tools And Technology Trends"
abstract: "Artificial Intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed the way individuals, organizations, and educational institutions perform tasks, solve problems, and make decisions. The increasing availability of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, GitHub Copilot, Midjourney, DALL-E, Grammarly, and Notion AI has significantly influenced areas including education, software development, content creation, research, design, and productivity. This study examines the current trends in the adoption and usage of AI tools, with a focus on understanding user preferences, purposes of AI usage, frequency of adoption, perceived benefits, and their impact on productivity and academic or professional performance. The study also explores emerging technology trends such as generative AI, AI-assisted programming, multimodal AI, automated content generation, and intelligent productivity systems. Survey-based data is analyzed using data analytics and machine learning techniques to identify patterns and relationships among different factors. The findings provide insights into how AI technologies are being adopted and how they are shaping modern workflows, learning practices, and decision-making. The study highlights the growing importance of responsible and effective AI usage while identifying opportunities and challenges associated with the rapid evolution of AI technologies."

title: Mapping Volcanic Facies for Critical Mineral Exploration Through Seismic Attributes and Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Critical minerals (CM) are essential for emerging technologies; however, their exploration remains challenging because they occur in complex geological settings and often exhibit weak seismic expression. Volcanic facies (VF) are one of their sources of occurrence, where minerals such as lead, cobalt, copper, and nickel often accumulate and scatter due to hydrothermal processes. This study presents a facies-specific machine learning (ML) workflow that integrates a multi-attribute approach with supervised and unsupervised ML, aiming to resolve VF in a complex geologic setting in the Otway Basin, South Australia. Twenty-two seismic attributes were calculated from which facies-specific attribute combinations were selected. Attributes were then used as input into Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) and Independent Component Analysis (ICA) to find sills, lava flows, and dykes, while Probabilistic Neural Networks (PNN) was applied for supervised classification of pyroclastics, mounds, and laccoliths that were not identified using unsupervised methods. Results indicate that SOM better discriminates between sills and lava and effectively identifies dyke geometry. ICA improved the delineation of dyke boundaries and enhanced the contrast between the intrusions and the background medium, revealing features that were less distinct in SOM results. PNN successfully resolved complex features such as laccoliths. Our methodology demonstrates that specific attribute combinations processed through SOM, ICA, and PNN can effectively discriminate between closely related volcanic features that are structurally favorable for CM accumulation.

title: Towards Diagnostic Explainability in Workflow Verification via Shapley Attribution
abstract: Workflow mining produces hierarchical workflow models from event logs, yet it is often unclear why such models satisfy or violate logical properties, or how individual model elements influence these outcomes. This work explores diagnostic explainability in workflow verification through the lens of attribution. We outline an approach that translates mined workflow models into logical specifications, checks properties, such as satisfiability, liveness and safety using automated theorem provers and interprets verification outcomes via Shapley values from the cooperative game theory. This attribution-based perspective provides a diagnostic view of how different parts of a workflow model contribute to property satisfaction or violation, highlighting elements that are critical, redundant or potentially harmful with respect to formal properties. Preliminary results suggest that Shapley-based attribution may support an interpretable workflow analysis while revealing limitations and trade-offs relevant to future research in explainable verification.

title: Robust link prediction in heterogeneous graphs via diffusion-based generative fusion and relation-aware guidance
abstract: Link prediction in heterogeneous graphs, which captures both topological and semantic information in graph structures helps the discovery of meaningful relationships. However, several fundamental challenges of link prediction remain insufficiently addressed. First, real-world data are noisy, causing existing models to struggle with learning robust representations. Second, although fusing information from multiple relation types is a core component of heterogeneous graph learning, most existing methods rely on simple aggregation methods such as a weighted sum. Such naive fusion may lead to embeddings that stray from their underlying manifold structure, ultimately degrading the accuracy of link prediction. Moreover, each link type is not equally informative. To address these challenges, we propose a novel diffusion-based framework for heterogeneous graph link prediction (DiffHGLP). Our proposed framework leverages a diffusion model to jointly denoise and fuse multi-relational information in heterogeneous graphs and employs an attention-based guidance mechanism for selecting links with informative link types. Extensive experiments on three public benchmark datasets show that DiffHGLP consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Quantum augmented salp swarm algorithm with adaptive parameter control (QSSA-APC) for hybrid-CNN hyperparameter tuning in realistic applications
abstract: In this study, a Quantum-Augmented Salp Swarm Algorithm with Adaptive Parameter Control (QSSA-APC) is presented as a novel optimization framework for effective hyperparameter tuning of Hybrid-CNN models in practical applications. The suggested method improves the convergence and optimization quality of the current Salp swarm algorithm (SSA) by balancing exploration and exploitation through the combination of quantum-inspired exploration and adaptive parameter control. Benchmark functions from IEEE CEC 2017, CEC 2020, and CEC 2022 under 50, 100, 10 and 20-dimensional problem spaces which span over unimodal, multimodal, hybrid, and composite issue classes are used to thoroughly assess the approach. Statistical significance is confirmed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank, Friedman and Holm post-hoc tests, supported by Cliff’s delta effect size analysis. Typical optimization measures, and convergence behavior are all part of performance analysis. Additionally, across a number of real-world image datasets, the suggested hybrid CNN–Transformer model modified by QSSA-APC shows appreciable gains in performance metrics and convergence analysis. The efficiency, higher robustness and scalability of QSSA-APC as a dependable metaheuristic optimizer for intricate, high-dimensional learning and engineering optimization problems are demonstrated by these results which proves it as a potential tool for realistic hybrid CNN hyperparameter optimization in challenging tasks.

title: Reading the Room: Foundations, Design, and Challenges of Normative Competence in LLMs
abstract: Human communities are governed by normative systems: shared standards that produce \textit{norms} dictating acceptable behavior, enforced through community sanctioning. Aligning increasingly autonomous AI systems with these norms is a central alignment challenge, complicated by the fact that norms are vast in number, change quickly, and are often arbitrary (e.g., dress or language conventions). Thus, alignment requires \textit{normative competence}: the ability to discern from interaction alone what norms a community enforces without relying on static pretrained knowledge. We introduce a multi-agent community debate setting, where access to debate is governed by synthetic norms, to study normative competence in isolation from pretraining exposure. We show that baseline LLM agents fail to learn norms even when doing so would improve their accuracy. We then experiment with various \textit{normative modules} -- architectural components for norm inference -- finding that norm-following is highly sensitive to both the style of norm and the model powering the normative module, suggesting a lack of generalizability. Furthermore, when idiosyncratic, non-normative behaviors accompany the true norm, LLM agents exhibit an unselective attribution failure: they indiscriminately copy idiosyncratic noise alongside enforced rules, a pattern that persists even when imitating unnecessary behaviors is explicitly penalized. To the best of our knowledge, our work is the first to operationalize and evaluate normative competence in LLMs, demonstrating that current AI systems excel at behavioral mimicry but lack the capacity to discern socially enforced order.

title: Informationally Decoupled Trajectory Design for Sim-to-Real System Identification
abstract: Sampling-based system identification estimates physically meaningful parameters by tuning a simulator to reproduce the target system dynamics, providing an interpretable approach to improving sim-to-real transfer. Yet when the collected trajectories do not distinguish the effects of different parameters, multiple parameter combinations can reproduce those trajectories, leading to unreliable parameter estimates. To address this challenge, we introduce an Informationally Decoupled Trajectory Design framework (IDTD), which formulates the objective for the exploration policy built on the Schur complement score derived from the Fisher information matrix. To faithfully reflect parameter separability in the exploration objective, IDTD normalizes the score against the per-parameter information, selects the most favorable trajectory segment for each parameter, and aggregates the resulting scores logarithmically. The optimized trajectory is therefore composed of complementary intervals, each exposing a distinct subset of parameters whose contribution to the motion over that interval can be attributed unambiguously. Across diverse simulation environments, ranging from a linear-dynamics system to the Go2 quadruped, G1 humanoid, and Crazyflie quadrotor, IDTD reduces the parameter identification error by 39.6% on average relative to the strongest prior active-exploration baseline and attains improved downstream policy transfer. Furthermore, we validate the proposed trajectory design on a real K1 humanoid, demonstrating that the resulting identified parameters accurately capture the real-system dynamics.

title: A repeating sequence of simple rules creates a universal computer
abstract: We show that the Turing complete rule 110 in elementary cellular automata can be emulated by alternating three simple symmetric rules in space. As the constituent rules themselves are trivial, this shows that diversity alone can generate emergent phenomena. The rules cannot distinguish left from right, and the chirality of rule 110 is created by their arrangement. Random initial conditions lock on to rule 110 over 90% of the time, explained through the motion of domain walls between desynchronized regions. Adding random noise creates errors that seed domain walls, whose fraction scales with the square root of noise strength, explained through a simple rate equation. This points to a route to complexity through repeated, perturbed units, common in biology, and shows that in cellular automaton models of quantum field theory, broken symmetries such as parity need not be present in the local rules.

title: INNOVATSION TA'LIM MUHITIDA ROBOTOTEXNIKADAN FOYDALANISHGA TAYYORLASH TEXNOLOGIYASI

title: CONECTA: a preregistered paired comparison of hierarchical-supervisor and flat-mesh-swarm multi-agent orchestration on reliability, cost and governance audit completeness
abstract: MSc Individual Project (University of Huddersfield; student Raul Rodenas, supervisor Dr Quratul-ain Mahesar). Within-subject paired experiment on CRMArena-Pro single-turn B2B tasks (six families: PVI, NCR, NED, HTU, KQA, TII) comparing two multi-agent orchestration topologies built on the same model, tools, prompts and governance middleware: Arm A, a hierarchical supervisor (LangGraph supervisor-via-tools); Arm B, a flat-mesh swarm (langgraph-swarm handoffs). Target 180 complete pairs (minimum 150) plus an 18-pair pilot, AB/BA counterbalanced. Primary outcome: Audit-Trail Completeness (ATC, T4, Wilcoxon signed-rank, alpha .05). Secondary outcomes (Benjamini-Hochberg q=.05): task success (T1), tokens (T2), latency (T3), escalation emission under a common scenario-imposed obligation (T5), coordination failure (T6). Backbone: Google Gemini API gemma-4-26b-a4b-it (free tier), temperature 0. The full preregistration text (v1.1), analysis specification, governance event contract v4, MAST coding manual, sampling rule, sensitivity analysis and a reproducibility manifest are attached. Registered before the formal pilot; development-exposure is disclosed in the attached text.

title: Future Trends in Quantum Computing for Medical Research
abstract: The field of quantum computing is also no longer in its infancy but is now being used to transform the healthcare sector with unprecedented computing power; this power can be used to improve machine learning as well as increase the security measures, which will spawn future innovations. The chapter provides an overview of the new environment of quantum-enabled healthcare, especially concentrating on collision points between machine learning and quantum computing to speed up diagnostics, and advancements in tailored healthcare. The quantum-enhanced algorithms would unlock complex biomedical trends that are beyond the capability of classical systems. Simultaneously, quantum cryptography is a security framework capable of providing strong security solutions that are needed to protect sensitive patient data in a healthcare environment that is becoming more digitized. With further development of quantum hardware and algorithms, they are likely to be incorporated in clinical practices, which will bring additional accuracy, efficiency, and ethical practices to medical research and practice. The chapter introduces the recent innovations and radical applications and discusses the issues that will have to be overcome to utilize the possibility of quantum-computing in healthcare to the fullest. Fused with artificial intelligence and secure health informatics, the study work predicts that there will come a time when smart medicine will be more intelligent as well as safer and predictive. The final part looks out into the future and shows how quantum advances could eventually transform the current healthcare paradigms, thereby sparking a new scientific discovery and human health renaissance.

title: Optimal Diffractive Focusing of Vortex Beams
abstract: We formulate diffractive ring focusing of paraxial beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) through a finite circular aperture as a variational optimization problem. For a fixed topological charge, we determine the real-valued radial pupil that maximizes the intensity at a prescribed ring radius and propagation distance under a normalization constraint on the input field. The resulting problem admits an exact analytical solution: the optimal pupil combines the familiar Fresnel phase structure with an OAM-dependent Bessel radial modulation, and the associated eigenvalue yields a rigorous upper bound on the achievable ring intensity. We further analyze the lens-assisted configuration and derive a simple bound that allows direct comparison between diffractive and refractive vortex focusing. The theory also provides a quantitative framework for evaluating the performance of practical mask designs, including binary Fresnel-Bessel zone plates and amplitude-weighted pupils. We have experimentally tested our predictions in the optical domain by implementing the corresponding vortex beam pupils and comparing their propagation and focusing performance with the optimal solution. Our results establish the vortex-beam analogue of optimal amplitude-only focusing and identify the fundamental limits governing diffractive concentration of structured waves

abstract: Rapid and accurate prediction of urban wind and temperature fields is important for urban microclimate design and climate adaptation. Large-eddy simulation (LES) effectively resolves these instantaneous fields, but its application is limited in iterative design of urban microclimate applications due to high computational cost. Existing regressive data-driven models offers quick outputs, but they produce only deterministic point predictions that inherently fail to represent turbulent stochasticity. This paper adopts a novel generative framework of Conditional Flow Matching (CFM) that uses building geometry and mean flow as guidance to generate plausible three-dimensional instantaneous velocity and temperature fields for urban microclimate in seconds. To overcome the GPU memory bottleneck of pixel space 3D generation, the model operates in parallel on overlapping pixel space through a shared-noise initialization that preserves high spatial continuity of flow structure across the entire domain. Against reference LES data, the CFM surrogate can rapidly and accurately restore the first-order statistics with Normalized Root Mean Square Error (NRMSE) of 2.99% for wind and 1.77% for temperature, second-order turbulence metrics with NRMSE of 7.17% for wind and 8.84% for temperature, turbulent kinetic energy with NRMSE of 7%, probability density function and vertical profiles in representative locations. Wind engineering application of local gust prediction demonstrate that the speed and accuracy of CFM, supporting the use of generative AI for making turbulence-aware resilient urban design and climate adaptation more computationally feasible.

title: MSU Team at the Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge 2026: Grounded Artifact Evidence for Deepfake Detection
abstract: Recent advances in generative image models have made many manipulated images highly realistic, raising the need for detectors that are not only accurate but also able to provide visual evidence for their decisions. In this paper, we present our solution to the Explainable Deepfake Detection Challenge [2] on the XPlainVerse dataset [1], where systems are required to predict whether an image is real or fake and generate both complex and simple explanations grounded in visible forensic cues. Our method follows a modular detection-and-explanation design. For the real/fake decision, we build a multi-backbone detector that combines several DINOv3 models with Mesorch manipulation-localization features, bringing together pretrained visual representations, DCT-aware cues, and multi-scale forensic information. To inject explanation evidence into the detector, we use a Grounding-DINO-based pseudo-mask generation pipeline that converts local artifact descriptions from training explanations into weak patch- level supervision for an Artifact Evidence Map. We further introduce a local patch-level contrastive objective that separates artifact and authenticity evidence in the detector feature space without requiring paired images or pixel-level manipulation masks. For language output, we use class-conditional Qwen3-VL models to generate complex explanations for fake and real predictions, followed by a GRPO-optimized text simplification model. The proposed methods were trained and evaluated on the challenge subset of XPlainVerse. On the full test split, our submission achieves 0.9349 detection accuracy, 0.5571 explanation score, and a 0.7456 final challenge score.

title: Enhancing Multi-Region Stylization with Interior-Guided Boundary Repair
abstract: Region-based neural style transfer enables fine-grained artistic control by allowing independent stylization of semantic image regions. However, compositing these regions often leads to boundary artifacts, degrading visual quality. We propose Interior-Guided Boundary Repair (IGBR), a lightweight and model-agnostic method that improves boundary handling in multi-region stylization. IGBR repairs boundary pixels using interior-guided propagation and applies inward, distance-based blending restricted to object-background boundaries, preventing inter-object style leakage. The method is derived from a region-wise constrained formulation with a closed-form solution and can be seamlessly integrated into existing stylization pipelines without retraining. To evaluate efficiency of our IGBR, we introduce quantitative metrics that measure boundary consistency, gradient artifacts, inter-object leakage, and interior preservation without requiring annotated stylized images. Our experiments and evaluations demonstrate that the proposed IGBR consistently produces plausible boundaries, outperforming prior blending techniques in boundary consistency, gradient stability, and interior preservation. The code is available at https://github.com/Son-SDT/IGBR.

title: FaceKit: a Toolkit for Interpretable Facial Phenotyping, Synthetic Image Generation and Privacy Analysis in Rare Diseases
abstract: Many rare genetic diseases are associated with recognizable craniofacial features. However, traditional approaches for describing facial morphology rely largely on qualitative clinical observation and free-text descriptions, which are often subjective, non-standardized, and difficult to reproduce across observers and institutions. Although the Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) provides controlled terms for describing facial features, these terms are typically categorical rather than quantitative and may vary depending on examiner experience and interpretation. Here, we present FaceKit, a computational framework for quantitative facial phenotyping from frontal facial photographs. FaceKit extracts standardized measurements of facial landmarks and derived 120 morphological features, then reports feature-level z-scores representing deviation from population reference distributions. The reference distributions are built from the FairFace dataset spanning diverse ancestral groups. We evaluated FaceKit on a curated subset of the GestaltMatcher Database covering 50 rare-disease cohorts. In addition to quantitative facial analysis, FaceKit includes synthetic facial image generation to support rare disease model development and data augmentation. We also performed privacy evaluation to assess whether synthetic images reveal identifiable information from real patient photographs and could compromise patient privacy. Across disease case studies, FaceKit-derived quantitative measurements captured known facial features associated with rare genetic disorders and provided objective support for clinical phenotyping. Together, these results establish FaceKit as a useful tool for quantitative phenotyping, and has the potential to improve rare disease diagnosis, support genotype-phenotype studies, and enable more reproducible clinical characterization across diverse patient populations.

title: Recovery or Repetition? Feedback Policy and Verbatim Relay in a Two-Agent Language-Model Loop
abstract: When a language model breaks an instruction and later appears to follow it again, the return can come from re-applying the rule or from reproducing text that already satisfies it. We separate these two sources in a two-agent loop built on a frozen Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct model. Both agents carry the same system rule, to write every word in capital letters, and one agent is asked to switch to lowercase. From an identical failed state on each of thirty prompts, four continuation policies are compared: plain forwarding to the partner, forwarding with a topic-continuation request, forwarding with the same lowercase request, and a repeated fixed reminder. Final-window adherence of the perturbed agent is 9/30, 10/30, 0/30 and 30/30, and both pre-specified paired contrasts hold after Holm adjustment (p = 0.0020 and p = 1.9 × 10−6). The complete text record explains these counts. The loop copies before any perturbation: in 27 of 30 prompts all six baseline answers are one identical string. After the perturbation, 20 of 21 first returns to capitals in the live loop are character-exact copies of the partner’s previous message, including all 19 that lead to final-window success; in 8 of the 10 topic-continuation successes the copied text is the agent’s own answer from before the perturbation; and 116 of 120 trajectories end on a constant string. The fixed reminder succeeds on every prompt with only 21 distinct strings across 330 outputs, 292 of which begin with the acknowledgement “SURE, I WILL CONTINUE”. Feedback policy decides which text circulates, and the format score reports the case of that text. Claims that an interactive agent has recovered a rule should therefore be tested on content it must newly compose. This record contains the preprint (PDF and LaTeX source) together with a complete reproduction package: all 2,612 model calls as raw records with full message histories and token ids, the executed notebook, the frozen protocol and generation configuration, an independent second audit implementation, the excluded numerical-fault batch (provenance only), the earlier exploratory study (unverified, provenance only), analysis and figure scripts, and per-file SHA256 checksums. The full chain reruns from the saved records on CPU in about twenty seconds, with no GPU and no model download. title: The Ladder of Truncation G: Categorical Unification—A Diagonalization Witness of Three Truncation Traditions in the Category of Sets
abstract: Three mutually disjoint mathematical traditions each record different fibers ofthe same event: the Cayley–Dickson construction exhibits zero divisors at the sedenions; a finite-capacity description system, when faced with a growing state space,is forced to merge distinguishable states; and a sufficiently strong formal systemcannot express its own truth predicate internally. This paper gives a categorytheoretic framework that unifies the three as a diagonalization witness in the category of sets, and precisely delimits the boundary of the unification. The frameworkhas five parts. The first part axiomatizes the category of weighted constraint networks: objects are weighted networks, morphisms are weight-preserving maps, andverification of closure under composition is elementary algebra. The second partgives rigorous constructions of the three towers and the exact identities of their respective witness maps: the inclusion maps of the algebraic tower are all monomorphisms, and the truncation witness is the non-injectivity of the left multiplicationoperator at the sedenions; the descriptive tower is explicitly constructed from analphabet, a description sequence, and a quotient map, and its truncation witnessis the non-injectivity of the description map forced by the pigeonhole principle;the inclusion translations of the syntactic tower are all monomorphisms, and itstruncation witness is the internal evaluation map negated by Lawvere’s theorem.The third part is the main theorem: three faithful comparison functors reflect thethree witness events respectively into explicit element constructions in the category of sets; the literal form of the first two events is non-diagonal kernel pairsaccommodating wandering kernel pairs, and the literal form of the third event is adiagonalization witness; the three share the Cantor diagonal schema. The fourthpart is the structural theorem: the rigid kernel theorem (a monotone sequenceof nonnegative integers must stabilize after finitely many steps, a purely ordinalargument) is proved in full; the functoriality of coalescence in birth-death operators is proved on the category of partitioned networks, while splitting and rewiringare registered as explicitly conditionalized propositions. The fifth part gives series coordinates: each component of this paper is docked one by one back to theconceptual chain of the six preceding papers A–F, closing the transmission of theseries. The paper distinguishes four knowledge layers: proved theorems, explicitconstructions, machine-checked evidence, and open conjectures; it does not claim1 that the three residues are isomorphic to one another, and locates unity at the levelof the diagonalization event.

title: Analisis Sentimen Berbasis Aspek Menggunakan Hybrid IndoBERT-Conv1D-BiLSTM Pada Program Makan Bergizi Gratis
abstract: This study analyzes public sentiment toward the Free Nutritious Meal Program (MBG) using an Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) approach on X (Twitter) data. A hybrid IndoBERT-Conv1D-BiLSTM model is proposed to classify sentiment across six MBG aspects. A total of 16,227 tweets were collected and automatically labeled using an Indonesian RoBERTa model, resulting in 14,756 tweets for training. After Random Oversampling, the model achieved a validation accuracy of 91.82%, a test accuracy of 91.10%, and a macro F1-score of 0.91. Compared with IndoBERT-only, CNN-only, BiLSTM-only, and SVM with TF-IDF, the proposed model achieved the best performance. The findings indicate that the proposed model is effective for aspect-based sentiment analysis and supports more comprehensive policy evaluation.

title: Integrating fuzzy neural networks and elastic weight consolidation for continual learning under non-stationary data streams
abstract: Neuro-fuzzy systems combine neural network learning with fuzzy logic to robustly represent qualitative, uncertain, and imprecise knowledge, making them especially effective for data mining and knowledge discovery. With ongoing digitalization, the volume and velocity of data streams have increased, creating a pressing need for neuro-fuzzy methods that operate reliably in non-stationary environments. While conventional neuro-fuzzy models exhibit strong performance on individual tasks, they struggle to adapt in dynamic environments where task distributions evolve over time, leading to significant forgetting of previously learned knowledge. To address this limitation, a novel approach that combines Fuzzy Neural Networks (FNN) with Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC) is proposed to address catastrophic forgetting in continual learning scenarios. The Fuzzy Radial Basis Function Neural Networks (FRBFNN) form fuzzy neural networks, which represent a class of fuzzy neural systems that combine the reasoning mechanism of fuzzy inference with the learning capability of neural networks. By leveraging this fusion structure, FRBFNN are particularly effective in modeling complex and highly nonlinear relationships within data. The EWC mechanism is employed to preserve knowledge by restricting changes to parameters critical for previously learned tasks. Furthermore, the fuzzy rule parameters—including centers, widths, and membership functions—are designed to evolve dynamically, enabling self-organization in response to new data distributions. This method addresses a key gap in existing research, where neuro-fuzzy models lack the capacity for continuous learning. Experimental results demonstrate that EWCFNN outperforms conventional neuro-fuzzy models, highlighting its effectiveness in mitigating catastrophic forgetting and interpretability.
